entries.hint2: Many bears do this in a cozy den.
entries.fact: Some animals rest all winter and wake in spring.

entries.hint: A spiky desert giant with bendy arms.
entries.hint2: It grows in the Mojave Desert in the USA.
entries.fact: It is a kind of yucca that grows in dry, sunny deserts.

entries.hint: To travel far to find a better place for the season.
entries.hint2: Geese do this each autumn.
entries.fact: Many birds fly south when winter comes.

entries.hint: A natural solid found in rocks, like quartz.
entries.hint2: Salt and gold are examples.
entries.fact: Plants take small amounts from the soil.

entries.hint: A little bit of wetness in soil or air.
entries.hint2: Damp soil has plenty of it.
entries.fact: Plants drink it up through their roots.

entries.hint: A very tall hill with a high peak.
entries.hint2: Snow often sits at the top.
entries.fact: The tops of tall mountains are often cool, even in summer.

entries.hint: A soft fungus shaped like a little umbrella.
entries.hint2: It pops up in damp woods.
entries.fact: Mushrooms are not plants. They belong to a group called fungi.

entries.hint: A spiky tropical fruit with a leafy crown.
entries.hint2: It is yellow inside, sweet and juicy.
entries.fact: A plant can take up to two years to grow just one of these fruits.

entries.hint: A scaly brown seed holder that falls from some evergreens.
entries.hint2: Squirrels nibble the seeds tucked between its scales.
entries.fact: Many open their scales in dry weather and close them when it is damp.

entries.hint: A jug-shaped green cup that traps bugs.
entries.hint2: Its slippery cup holds a sweet liquid.
entries.fact: Its cup-shaped leaves catch bugs for a meal.

entries.hint: A wide, flat grassland.
entries.hint2: Bison roam these plains.
entries.fact: Tall grasses and wildflowers wave in the wind.

entries.hint: An animal that hunts other animals for food.
entries.hint2: A hawk is one.
entries.fact: Ladybugs hunt tiny aphids, which helps garden plants.

entries.hint: A masked animal with a ringed tail.
entries.hint2: It has a black mask across its eyes and comes out at night.
entries.fact: Raccoons have very sensitive front paws that help them feel for food.

entries.hint: The amount of water that drops from the clouds.
entries.hint2: A gauge in the garden measures it.
entries.fact: Plants need it to grow.

entries.hint: A young tree that is still thin and small.
entries.hint2: An oak starts as one.
entries.fact: A tiny tree can grow into a giant over many years.

entries.hint: A straw figure that stands in a field.
entries.hint2: It wears old clothes and a hat.
entries.fact: Farmers put one up to keep birds away from seeds.

entries.hint: A hard, curly case a sea animal grows to cover its soft body.
entries.hint2: Hold it to your ear and listen.
entries.fact: Seashells come in many shapes, like spirals and fans.

entries.hint: Spring, summer, autumn and winter.
entries.hint2: There are four of these in a year.
entries.fact: Earth tilts as it travels around the sun, which brings four of these.

entries.hint: A plant-like growth that floats and sways in the ocean.
entries.hint2: Some kinds are wrapped around sushi.
entries.fact: Kelp is a kind of seaweed that can grow very tall under the sea.

entries.hint: Touch its leaves and they fold up like tiny hands.
entries.hint2: It is also called the touch-me-not.
entries.fact: Its leaves fold shut when touched, then open again soon.

entries.hint: A tiny, six-sided crystal of ice.
entries.hint2: It drifts down in winter.
entries.fact: Most snowflakes have six sides or six points.

entries.hint: A small brown bird that hops in gardens.
entries.hint2: It chirps from the hedge.
entries.fact: It likes to eat seeds and crumbs.

entries.hint: A bushy-tailed animal that buries nuts.
entries.hint2: It leaps from branch to branch in the park.
entries.fact: Some buried nuts are never dug up and grow into new trees.

entries.hint: What leaves use to make their food.
entries.hint2: Leaves turn toward it all day.
entries.fact: Plants soak it up to grow.

entries.hint: When the sun first appears in the morning.
entries.hint2: Roosters crow at this time.
entries.fact: The sky glows pink and orange at dawn.

entries.hint: The happy weather word for a clear, bright day.
entries.hint2: Plants stretch toward it.
entries.fact: Light from the sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.

entries.hint: A baby frog with a tail that swims.
entries.hint2: It lives in a pond.
entries.fact: It grows legs and becomes a frog.

entries.hint: A curly little thread that helps a vine climb.
entries.hint2: Pea plants use it to grab a fence.
entries.fact: Peas, grapes and cucumbers all climb with these.

entries.hint: The loud rumble you hear after lightning.
entries.hint2: Clouds make this big sound.
entries.fact: Lightning heats the air and the air booms.

entries.hint: A spinning funnel of wind.
entries.hint2: It twirls down from a storm cloud.
entries.fact: Weather scientists watch the sky for these swirling winds.

entries.hint: A frame that helps climbing plants grow tall.
entries.hint2: Roses and beans can climb it.
entries.fact: It is made of wood or wire with crisscross bars.

entries.hint: A mountain that can bubble up hot melted rock.
entries.hint2: Some have a crater at the top.
entries.fact: Hot rock from inside Earth is called lava.

entries.hint: A soggy place beside a pond or stream.
entries.hint2: Frogs and herons love it.
entries.fact: Marshes and swamps are this kind of place.

entries.hint: A huge slide of snow rushing down a mountain.
entries.hint2: Skiers watch out for this on steep snowy slopes.
entries.fact: Deep snow on a steep slope can suddenly slide all at once.

entries.hint: The tweets and trills heard at dawn.
entries.hint2: Robins and wrens fill the morning with it.
entries.fact: Many birds sing most at dawn, in what is called the dawn chorus.

entries.hint: A garden plant with pink flowers shaped like valentines that dangle like lockets.
entries.hint2: Its flowers hang in a row on a curved stem, each with a tiny white drop at the tip.
entries.fact: It blooms in spring, with each flower dangling from an arching stem.

entries.hint: A big green pond animal with a deep, booming croak.
entries.hint2: It sits on a lily pad and calls very low and loud.
entries.fact: A bullfrog's deep call can be heard far across a pond.

entries.hint: A small, shiny yellow wildflower in grassy fields.
entries.hint2: Hold it under your chin to see a yellow glow.
entries.fact: Its petals are so shiny that they bounce yellow light back.

entries.hint: A fuzzy, crawling bug that will grow into a butterfly or moth.
entries.hint2: It munches leaves all day.
entries.fact: A caterpillar grows so fast that it must shed its skin several times.

entries.hint: A small daisy-like flower used to make a calming tea.
entries.hint2: Its tea is often sipped before bedtime.
entries.fact: Its flowers smell a little like apples.

entries.hint: A small striped animal that stuffs seeds into its cheeks.
entries.hint2: It is like a tiny squirrel with stripes on its back.
entries.fact: It carries food in stretchy cheek pouches to its burrow.

entries.hint: The edge where land meets the sea.
entries.hint2: Cliffs, coves and beaches run along it.
entries.fact: Waves slowly reshape the land along the sea, grain by grain.

entries.hint: A smooth old log that floats in and washes up on shore.
entries.hint2: Waves roll it along the beach.
entries.fact: Water and sand polish driftwood until it feels smooth.

entries.hint: A place where a river meets the sea.
entries.hint2: Fresh water and salty water mix here.
entries.fact: Many baby fish grow up in the calm waters of an estuary.

entries.hint: A tree that keeps its needles or leaves all year.
entries.hint2: Fir and pine trees look fresh all winter long.
entries.fact: Many pine and fir trees keep their needles through the cold months.

entries.hint: Soil that is rich and full of what plants need.
entries.hint2: Good garden dirt is this, so seeds grow well.
entries.fact: Soil gets richer when old leaves and bits of plants mix into it.

entries.hint: Having a sweet smell.
entries.hint2: Lavender and roses are like this.
entries.fact: Flowers make sweet smells to invite bees and butterflies.

entries.hint: A huge round leaf that floats on a still pool and can hold a small child.
entries.hint2: Its flat leaves are like green rafts.
entries.fact: Its round leaves can grow wider than a grown-up is tall.

entries.hint: A green insect with long back legs that jumps.
entries.hint2: It chirps in tall meadows in summer.
entries.fact: It can leap many times its own body length.

entries.hint: A glass building that keeps plants cozy and warm.
entries.hint2: Gardeners grow seedlings here in early spring.
entries.fact: Sunlight comes through the glass walls and warms the air inside.

entries.hint: A ball of ice that falls from a storm cloud.
entries.hint2: These icy pellets bounce off the ground.
entries.fact: Hail grows in layers as it is tossed up and down inside a cloud.

entries.hint: A long line of bushes that grows along a field.
entries.hint2: Birds build nests in this green wall.
entries.fact: Hedges give birds and small animals a safe path and a cozy home.

entries.hint: A climbing plant with sweet, trumpet-shaped flowers.
entries.hint2: Bees and hummingbirds sip the sweet nectar from its blossoms.
entries.fact: Many kinds smell sweetest in the evening, when moths come to visit.

entries.hint: A tiny flier that hovers to sip nectar.
entries.hint2: Its wings move so fast they blur.
entries.fact: A hummingbird can flap its wings dozens of times each second.

entries.hint: A big flower from South Africa that looks like a pink crown.
entries.hint2: It is the national flower of South Africa.
entries.fact: The king protea has the biggest flower head of all the protea plants.

entries.hint: A wide view of hills, fields and trees.
entries.hint2: An artist might paint a scene of the countryside.
entries.fact: Farms, forests and rivers all help shape a landscape.

entries.hint: A giant spark that zaps between storm clouds and the ground.
entries.hint2: You see this flash before you hear the boom.
entries.fact: Its flash is hotter than the surface of the sun.

entries.hint: An evergreen with spiky, scale-like leaves that twist along its branches.
entries.hint2: It comes from the mountains of Chile and has twisty branches.
entries.fact: Its name comes from a joke that even a monkey would be puzzled how to climb its prickly branches.

entries.hint: The soft silver glow that shines on a dark garden after sunset.
entries.hint2: Owls hunt by it.
entries.fact: The moon makes no glow of its own; it reflects sunlight.

entries.hint: Awake and busy at night.
entries.hint2: Owls and bats are like this.
entries.fact: Owls have big eyes that help them see in the dark.

entries.hint: A round red fruit packed with juicy seeds.
entries.hint2: Each little red jewel inside holds a seed.
entries.fact: One fruit can hold hundreds of seeds.

entries.hint: A slow animal covered in sharp quills.
entries.hint2: Its spiky coat keeps hungry animals away.
entries.fact: A porcupine can have thousands of quills.

entries.hint: A giant flower from the rainforest with no leaves, roots or stem.
entries.hint2: It is one of the biggest flowers in the world.
entries.fact: One rafflesia flower can grow about one meter across.

entries.hint: A thick, warm jungle where showers fall almost every day.
entries.hint2: Many bright parrots and frogs call it home.
entries.fact: Rainforests are home to more kinds of plants and animals than almost anywhere else.

entries.hint: The sloping ground along the edge of a stream.
entries.hint2: Ducks rest on the grass beside the water.
entries.fact: Plants along a stream edge hold the soil in place with their roots.

entries.hint: A woody herb with needle-like leaves and a piney smell.
entries.hint2: Cooks put it on roast potatoes.
entries.fact: Bees love its small blue flowers.

entries.hint: A very old kind of plant with a stout trunk and a crown of stiff, feathery leaves.
entries.hint2: Its leaves look like big green feathers, and it grows in warm places.
entries.fact: Cycads like the sago palm have grown on Earth since the age of dinosaurs.

entries.hint: A small, smooth-skinned animal that looks like a lizard but lives near water.
entries.hint2: It is an amphibian with a long tail, like a newt.
entries.fact: Many salamanders can grow back a tail or even a leg.

entries.hint: A small bird that runs along the beach on thin legs.
entries.hint2: It pokes its long beak in wet ground for tiny food.
entries.fact: Sandpipers chase the waves in and out as they look for food.

entries.hint: A flower with a pouch-shaped petal that looks like a tiny shoe.
entries.hint2: Its bloom looks like a shoe for a fairy.
entries.fact: Bees climb into the slipper-shaped pouch and then wriggle out past the pollen.

entries.hint: A tiny white flower that pokes up through late winter frost.
entries.hint2: Its white bells hang down like little lamps.
entries.fact: It is one of the first flowers to bloom each year.

entries.hint: A plant with thick, juicy leaves that hold water.
entries.hint2: Aloe and jade plants are this kind.
entries.fact: Succulents store water in their leaves so they can go many days between drinks.

entries.hint: One long, thick part of a plant that grows straight down into soil.
entries.hint2: A carrot is a good example.
entries.fact: A dandelion has a deep root that reaches far into the soil.

entries.hint: A small glass garden for tiny plants.
entries.hint2: You can grow moss and ferns in a jar like this.
entries.fact: A closed glass garden can water itself, because moisture drips back to the soil.

entries.hint: A dry plant that breaks free and rolls across the plains in the wind.
entries.hint2: You see it bounce along in western movies.
entries.fact: As it rolls, it scatters its seeds across the land.

entries.hint: A stream that tumbles over a high cliff.
entries.hint2: Rivers do this when the ground drops away.
entries.fact: Some waterfalls make a soft mist that can create a rainbow.

entries.hint: A big green-striped fruit with sweet red flesh.
entries.hint2: You spit out the black seeds on a hot day.
entries.fact: It is mostly water, which makes it a great summer snack.

entries.hint: A bloom that grows by itself without a gardener.
entries.hint2: Meadows are dotted with these in summer.
entries.fact: Wildflowers grow from seeds that wind and birds carry about.

entries.hint: Animals and plants that live free in nature.
entries.hint2: Think of deer, birds and foxes in the woods.
entries.fact: Parks and forests give homes to many kinds of animals.

entries.hint: A place with many trees growing close together.
entries.hint2: Squirrels and deer live among the trees here.
entries.fact: Fallen leaves in a woodland slowly turn back into rich soil.

entries.hint: A bird that drums on tree trunks with its beak.
entries.hint2: Tap tap tap! It looks for bugs inside bark.
entries.fact: Its stiff tail feathers prop it up as it clings to a tree.

entries.hint: An animal like a frog that lives part in water and part on land.
entries.hint2: Frogs, toads and newts all belong to this group.
entries.fact: Many of them start life in water, then grow lungs and legs.

entries.hint: Any plant that makes flowers and keeps its seeds inside fruit.
entries.hint2: Roses, apple trees and grasses are all this kind of plant.
entries.fact: Most kinds of plants on Earth today are flowering plants.

entries.hint: A garden full of many kinds of trees.
entries.hint2: You can visit one to learn tree names.
entries.fact: Some of these gardens hold thousands of different kinds of trees.

entries.hint: An animal with jointed legs and a hard outer shell.
entries.hint2: Spiders, crabs and insects all belong to this big group.
entries.fact: Its name means jointed foot.

entries.hint: The blanket of air that wraps around Earth.
entries.hint2: Weather happens in the lowest layer of it.
entries.fact: It keeps Earth warm and blocks much of the sun's harsh rays.

entries.hint: The huge variety of living things on Earth.
entries.hint2: All the different plants, animals and tiny life in one place.
entries.fact: A spoonful of healthy soil can hold millions of tiny living things.

entries.hint: Describes living things that make their own glow.
entries.hint2: Fireflies and some deep-sea fish are this way.
entries.fact: Some mushrooms glow softly in the dark woods.

entries.hint: A dark bloom with long whiskers and wide, wing-shaped petals.
entries.hint2: It is so dark it looks like night, and it grows in shady forests.
entries.fact: This flower comes from the warm forests of Southeast Asia.

entries.hint: A scientist who studies plants.
entries.hint2: This person might name a brand new flower.
entries.fact: Botanists have named more than 300,000 kinds of plants.

entries.hint: Colors or shapes that help a creature blend in.
entries.hint2: A stick bug uses this to look like a twig.
entries.fact: Some moths look just like tree bark when they rest.

entries.hint: Describes a plant that catches and digests insects.
entries.hint2: A Venus flytrap is this kind of plant.
entries.fact: Plants like these grow in soil that has very few nutrients, so bugs give them extra food.

entries.hint: A deep red bloom that smells like something sweet.
entries.hint2: Its scent is like warm cocoa.
entries.fact: On warm summer days its flowers smell a little like chocolate.

entries.hint: A palm that grows the biggest seed in the world.
entries.hint2: Its seed is so big and heavy that you need two hands to lift it.
entries.fact: One seed can weigh more than a bowling ball.

entries.hint: When water vapor cools and turns back into drops.
entries.hint2: It makes droplets on the outside of a cold glass.
entries.fact: Clouds form when water vapor cools into tiny droplets.

entries.hint: Describes trees that grow cones and needles.
entries.hint2: Pine and spruce forests are this type.
entries.fact: Most of these trees keep their needles all winter.

entries.hint: Taking good care of nature so it stays healthy.
entries.hint2: Protecting forests, rivers and animals is part of it.
entries.fact: Planting trees and keeping rivers clean are ways to help nature.

entries.hint: A group of stars that makes a picture in the night sky.
entries.hint2: Orion the hunter is a famous one.
entries.fact: Long ago, sailors used star pictures to find their way at sea.

entries.hint: The first seed leaf that pops out of a sprouting seed.
entries.hint2: Beans have two of these baby leaves.
entries.fact: Grasses have one seed leaf, while beans have two.

entries.hint: The work of growing crops and garden plants.
entries.hint2: Farmers do this with seeds, soil and care.
entries.fact: People have grown plants on farms for about ten thousand years.

entries.hint: A living thing that turns old leaves into soil.
entries.hint2: Mushrooms and tiny bacteria do this job.
entries.fact: Mushrooms break down fallen leaves and return food to the soil.

entries.hint: A deep rest that plants take in cold or dry times.
entries.hint2: Trees do this in winter, and then wake in spring.
entries.fact: Many bulbs rest underground until the weather turns warm.

entries.hint: How bats find bugs in the dark by listening to sound bounce back.
entries.hint2: Bats and dolphins use this sound trick.
entries.fact: A bat can find a tiny moth in the dark just by listening for echoes.

entries.hint: A scientist who studies how living things connect.
entries.hint2: This person looks at how plants, animals and soil fit together.
entries.fact: Ecologists often study ponds, forests and meadows.

entries.hint: A community of living things and the place they share.
entries.hint2: A pond with its fish, frogs and plants is one of these.
entries.fact: An ecosystem can be as small as a puddle or as big as an ocean.

entries.hint: Describes a kind of animal or plant that is rare and needs protecting.
entries.hint2: Pandas and some sea turtles have been on this list.
entries.fact: The giant panda was moved off this list in 2016 after people protected its forests.

entries.hint: A plant that grows on a tree branch instead of in soil.
entries.hint2: Some orchids and ferns live high up in the trees this way.
entries.fact: Many of these plants catch rain and mist straight from the air.

entries.hint: The hard outer shell that covers an insect's body.
entries.hint2: A crab and a beetle both wear this hard armor.
entries.fact: Insects shed this hard shell so they can grow bigger.

entries.hint: When a kind of animal or plant is gone from the wild for good.
entries.hint2: People protect rare animals and plants to stop this from happening.
entries.fact: People work to protect rare plants and animals, and some, like the bald eagle, have come back strong.

entries.hint: Food you add to soil to help plants grow.
entries.hint2: Gardeners sprinkle it around their flowers.
entries.fact: Compost is a natural kind that gardeners make at home.

entries.hint: A plant with white flowers that today grows in gardens, not in the wild.
entries.hint2: It is named for a famous American who flew a kite in a storm.
entries.fact: Its white flowers with golden centers open in late summer and autumn.

entries.hint: A pale bloom that seems to float in the air.
entries.hint2: It has no leaves and clings to swamp trees.
entries.fact: Its white flower has long thin tails that look like a frog's legs.

entries.hint: A plant with bare seeds, often held in cones.
entries.hint2: Pines, firs and ginkgo trees are this kind.
entries.fact: Its name means naked seed in Greek.

entries.hint: Describes a plant with soft green stems instead of wood.
entries.hint2: Daisies and mint are this type.
entries.fact: Herbaceous plants often grow new stems each spring.

entries.hint: An animal that eats plants and nothing else.
entries.hint2: Rabbits, deer and cows are this kind of eater.
entries.fact: A cow's stomach has four parts to help break down grass.

entries.hint: The art and science of growing garden plants.
entries.hint2: Gardeners and nursery workers practice this.
entries.fact: People have grown gardens for thousands of years.

entries.hint: Growing plants in water with no soil.
entries.hint2: The roots float in water full of plant food.
entries.fact: Some farms grow salad leaves in water and use less of it than fields do.

entries.hint: An animal with no backbone, like a worm or a snail.
entries.hint2: Insects, spiders and slugs are all this kind of animal.
entries.fact: Most kinds of animals on Earth have no backbone.

entries.hint: A climbing plant with turquoise flowers shaped like claws.
entries.hint2: Its glowing blue-green blooms hang down in long chains.
entries.fact: Bats visit this vine from the Philippines to sip its nectar.

entries.hint: An animal whose babies grow in a pouch.
entries.hint2: Kangaroos and koalas are this kind of animal.
entries.fact: A baby kangaroo, called a joey, is about the size of a jelly bean when it is born.

entries.hint: The big body change from caterpillar to butterfly.
entries.hint2: A tadpole turning into a frog goes through this.
entries.fact: A tadpole grows legs and its tail shrinks as it becomes a frog.

entries.hint: A small spot with its own weather, like a sunny wall.
entries.hint2: A cozy corner of the garden can be warmer than the rest.
entries.fact: A garden wall can make a warm pocket where tender plants grow well.

entries.hint: A living thing so tiny you need a lens to see it.
entries.hint2: Bacteria are this kind of very small life.
entries.fact: Some of them help turn milk into yogurt.

entries.hint: A gas that fills about four fifths of the air around us.
entries.hint2: Plants need it for green leaves, and clover helps add it to soil.
entries.fact: About four fifths of the air around us is this gas.

entries.hint: Something in food or soil that living things need to grow.
entries.hint2: Plants pull these up from the soil through their roots.
entries.fact: Plants need nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium most of all.

entries.hint: An animal that eats both plants and meat.
entries.hint2: Bears and people are this kind of eater.
entries.fact: Raccoons eat fruit, nuts, insects and fish.

entries.hint: A way of gardening that works with the land.
entries.hint2: It designs food gardens to look after themselves.
entries.fact: These gardens use plants, animals and water to help each other.

entries.hint: Ground that stays frozen all year round.
entries.hint2: It lies under the Arctic tundra.
entries.fact: Some of it has stayed frozen for thousands of years.

entries.hint: When a plant bends toward the light.
entries.hint2: A windowsill plant leans toward the glass.
entries.fact: The shady side of a stem grows faster, so the stem bends toward the light.

entries.hint: Any water that falls from clouds, like rain, snow or hail.
entries.hint2: Weather reports tell you the chance of this.
entries.fact: Snow, sleet, hail and rain are all kinds of it.

entries.hint: To make new plants from a cutting or a seed.
entries.hint2: Snip a stem, put it in water and watch roots grow.
entries.fact: Many houseplants grow roots when you put a cutting in water.

entries.hint: A giant mountain plant that makes a very tall flower spike.
entries.hint2: It grows high in the Andes, and its spike is taller than a house.
entries.fact: It can grow for eighty years or more before it blooms.

entries.hint: Sand, mud and tiny bits of rock carried by water.
entries.hint2: It settles on the bottom of a river or lake.
entries.fact: Layers of it, pressed down over long ages, can turn into rock.

entries.hint: The day with the longest or shortest daylight of the year.
entries.hint2: Midsummer and midwinter each have one.
entries.fact: It happens twice a year, in June and December.

entries.hint: Two living things helping each other live well.
entries.hint2: Bees and flowers are good partners like this.
entries.fact: Clownfish and sea anemones help each other in this way.

entries.hint: The science of naming and sorting living things into groups.
entries.hint2: It puts lions and tigers in the same cat family.
entries.fact: Every known plant has a two-part science name, like Bellis perennis for the daisy.

entries.hint: How a plant releases water vapor through its leaves.
entries.hint2: Water travels up from the roots and floats out into the air.
entries.fact: A big tree can send more than a hundred liters of water into the air on a summer day.

entries.hint: The layer of smaller plants beneath tall forest trees.
entries.hint2: Shade-loving ferns and shrubs grow here.
entries.fact: Many shy forest birds build nests in the understory.

entries.hint: Rich soil food made by worms eating scraps.
entries.hint2: Red wigglers turn kitchen peels into garden gold.
entries.fact: Worms can turn apple cores and leaves into rich soil for plants.

entries.hint: Land where rain flows downhill into the same river.
entries.hint2: All the streams in one valley join up.
entries.fact: Every raindrop that lands in a watershed ends up in the same river or lake.

entries.hint: When wind, rain and ice slowly crack and crumble rock.
entries.hint2: Tree roots can split stones this way too.
entries.fact: Over many years, it helps turn rock into soil.

entries.hint: An ancient tree found in a hidden canyon in Australia.
entries.hint2: Its family was known from fossils until a bushwalker found it in 1994.
entries.fact: Fewer than a hundred grown trees are known in the wild.
